text:
olivia: Quick report — the new App Router Next starter (examples/next-app-router-starter) is tripping up a few new users. When running on Vercel edge runtime the server actions example that exchanges a dev ephemeral token is returning 401s intermittently. Works fine in node dev. Anyone seen edge-only auth flakes?

ben: Edge behaves differently w.r.t cookies and incoming headers. Are you using cookie-based dev tokens or sending auth in an Authorization header?

olivia: Cookie-based dev token. Flow: client calls /api/session -> sets cookie, then a server action (app/actions/ask) reads cookies via headers and calls Redwood client. On Vercel edge the cookie sometimes isn't present in the action request. Happens ~1/15 page loads in dev and sometimes on preview deploys.

tara: Two immediate suspects: 1) App Router server actions run in a different fetch context and on edge the cookie jar handling can differ; 2) Vercel preview routing can strip SameSite or Secure flags if env not set.

frank: Can you paste the server action snippet?

olivia: Simplified: ```js
// app/actions/ask.js
export async function serverAction(formData) {
  const token = cookies().get('rd_token')?.value;
  if (!token) throw new Error('missing token');
  const client = new Redwood({ token });
  return client.generate({ prompt: formData.get('q') });
}
```

ben: Using cookies() from next/headers works in node runtime but edge env sometimes receives an empty header bag if the browser hasn't persisted the cookie or if the action is invoked via a client fetch instead of automatic form submission. Are users calling the action via fetch() or <form action=>?

olivia: Mostly via form action, but some examples show a client-side fetch for progressive enhancement. I reproduced it by swapping to fetch: sometimes the cookie header is missing.

tara: For the starter we should: (A) document App Router caveats in README (server actions vs fetch behavior); (B) add a dev-only fallback: if cookies().get missing then look for Authorization header and try to exchange server-side; (C) include a tiny helper that warns in the console and retries once with short jitter.

frank: I worry about changing example semantics. Keep production behavior unchanged. Make the fallback opt-in behind a dev flag (process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_EXAMPLES_DEV_HELPER) and only perform header fallback in non-prod.

ben: Also recommend the sample use a server->server token mint pattern as canonical: server action calls internal auth service (server side) to mint a token based on secure cookie, rather than relying on browser-set ephemeral cookies. Show both patterns in docs.

olivia: Agreed. I'll draft changes: (1) add examples/shared/app-router-dev-helpers.js with a function readToken({req, headers}) that in dev does small immediate retry and checks headers.Authorization, (2) update server action to call readToken, (3) add README/AppRouter.md explaining differences and when to use server->server mint.

tara: For the retry avoid sleeps in tests. Use a single immediate retry (check cookie/header again) and, if still missing, log a help message: "Dev cookie not found — try clearing browser cookies or use server-side mint." Keep logs debug level.

frank: Streaming note: we also need to show how to abort edge streams. The edge runtime doesn't support AbortController on the req the same way Node does. Add a section that shows both patterns and a safe fallback: if signal not present, ensure SDK supports iterator.return() cleanup and call it on when client disconnect is detected.

olivia: Good call. The starter currently uses the page route SSE pattern. I'll include an edge-safe stream example that checks for request.finalized or gracefully calls iterator.return() when available. Also add a comment linking to an SDK ticket for AbortSignal parity.

ben: For tests, mock cookies() and headers() deterministically. Do not rely on timing. In eval-harness add two unit tests: one where cookie present, one where cookie absent but Authorization header present. Assert proper behavior in both.

olivia: I'll open a PR with minimal changes and tests. PR will include: helper, README, two mock tests, and a dev-only log gate. I'll tag @tara and @frank for review.

ci-bot: Reminder: examples CI will run. Mark network calls as mocked. If preview deploys show cookie variance, keep the helper behind a dev flag to avoid surprising preview behavior.

docs-bot: Suggestion: also add a short troubleshooting snippet to the DX docs: "App Router token missing on edge — check SameSite/Secure cookie flags, proxy settings, or use server-side mint".

tara: Sounds great. One tiny nit: make the helper name explicit (readDevTokenFromHeadersOrCookies) so it's not accidentally used in prod. Also add a comment that App Router form actions behave differently than fetch() regarding cookies.

frank: Thanks — this should reduce onboarding tickets for users trying examples on Vercel. Please include a link to the SDK issue for signal/abort parity in the PR description.

olivia: PR opened: 3120000027-app-router-edge-token-helpers. Adding reviewers now. :rocket:

ben: Will review shortly. Thanks for consolidating this, Olivia. :thumbsup:
